question.prompt:
The adjacent sides of the decagon shown meet at right angles. What is its perimeter?

[Figure 1](figures/1997_AMC_12_Q02_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
We can find the perimeter without finding every individual side. Follow the boundary from the bottom-left vertex up the left side and around to the bottom-right vertex. The four horizontal segments along this route all go right, so together they span the same distance as the bottom side: \(12\). Thus all horizontal sides together have length \(12+12=24\).

Along the same route, the upward segments have lengths \(8\) and \(2\). Since the route starts and ends at the same height, the downward segments must also total \(8+2=10\). Therefore all vertical sides together have length \(10+10=20\).

Every side is either horizontal or vertical, so the perimeter is
\[
24+20=\boxed{44},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Combine lengths in each direction
